title: Introduce Elasticity Scribe and Deferred Burst Signing
author: Samir Patel
release_notes: Add Elasticity Scribe (audit trail for autoscaler decisions) and Deferred Burst Signing (cryptographically-signed temporary burst tokens). Backward compatible; opt-in via FleetElasticityPolicy CRD. Includes telemetry and dashboards for decision reasoning and burst accounting.
description: Motivation: Fleet autoscaling decisions are currently opaque to SRE/finance and hard to replay for incident postmortems. Bursts are granted by runtime heuristics without a signed provenance; downstream gateways cannot reliably attribute temporary capacity to a formal commitment. This PR introduces two related components: (1) Elasticity Scribe: an append-only, compact audit trail of autoscaler decisions (scale up/down, prewarm, deferred decommit) that captures inputs, chosen action, and rationale; (2) Deferred Burst Signing: a lightweight signing service that issues short-lived cryptographic tokens when the autoscaler authorizes temporary burst capacity. The signed token includes tenant id, committed delta, expiry, and a decision_id that links to the scribe entry. Design highlights: - Elasticity Scribe writes protobuff-style records to a configurable backend (default: compressed protobufs to the existing fleet-telemetry bucket). Records include timestamp, decision_id (UUID), contributors (utilization, queued tokens, headroom, prediction), chosen action, and confidence score. - Deferred Burst Signing exposes an internal-only gRPC endpoint used by the autoscaler; tokens are signed using the cluster key in KMS and include a verifiable HMAC and simple nonce to prevent replay. Gateways validate tokens before honoring burst capacity. - New CRD FleetElasticityPolicy: opt-in fields for scribe retention window, burst-signing enabled, and max-deferred-burst-duration. - Telemetry: counters/gauges (redwood_elasticity_decisions_total, redwood_elasticity_decision_latency_seconds, redwood_burst_signatures_issued_total, redwood_burst_signature_validation_failure_total) and labels to correlate tenant, pool, and decision_type. - Observability: Grafana dashboard and a LogQL quick query for postmortem analysis (decision timeline, queue correlation). Rollout plan: 1) Feature-gate off by default. 2) Canary in internal dedicated fleet for two weeks with scribe only (no enforced gating). 3) Enable burst signing in a single region with gateways updated to validate tokens for a subset of tenants (10% traffic). 4) Fleet-wide enable after 3 successful canaries and one incident-free billing cycle. Checklist: - [x] Prototype scribe writer and minimal storage adapter - [x] Deferred burst signing API + KMS integration - [x] Unit tests for scribe encoding/decoding and token validation - [x] E2E test in perf-canary harness (stable for 48 hours) - [x] Telemetry and dashboard definitions - [x] Docs: operations and upgrade notes - [x] Security review (key rotation and token TTL constraints) Backwards compatibility: Gateways that do not validate tokens will ignore the signed burst header; signing is additive and controlled by FleetElasticityPolicy. Impact to billing: this PR provides better attribution and does not change billing behavior until accounting hooks are switched on in a follow-up. Related: ENG-1839 (decision replay tooling), ENG-1942 (burst accounting schema).

review_comments: Ava Rodriguez (2025-10-14): Can we avoid writing raw tenant IDs into the scribe storage? Suggest hashing tenant ID with a salt to preserve privacy.
Author (Samir) (2025-10-14): Addressed in next push — added tenant_id_hash field and deprecated raw tenant write. Storage adapter now accepts an optional salt provider.
Lena Müller (2025-10-15): Are we confident KMS latency won't affect autoscaler critical path? Suggest using async signing with local cache for the canary.
Author (Samir) (2025-10-15): Implemented a short-lived signing cache and fall back to synchronous KMS only when cache miss. Added metrics to surface KMS latency.
Diego Fernandez (2025-10-16): Tests flaky in perf-canary; observed intermittent e2e failure when gateway validation timed out. Please add retry and backpressure guard.
Author (Samir) (2025-10-17): Added retry with jitter and tightened gateway validation deadline; re-ran canary, stable for 72 hours. Approving review.
Ava Rodriguez (2025-10-18): 2 approvals, security sign-off completed. Ready to merge.
ci_checks: unit-tests: fail (flaky on signer cache) — rerun
merge_outcome: Merged after 2 approvals and CI green. Feature gated off by default; rollout controlled via FleetElasticityPolicy.
notes_for_ops: Feature requires updating helm chart values to opt in: set fleetElasticity.policy.scribe.enabled=true and fleetElasticity.policy.burstSigning.enabled=true. KMS key ARN must be provided and rotated per org policy. Observe redwood_elasticity_decisions_total and redwood_burst_signatures_issued_total during canary. If gateways reject tokens, rollback by disabling burstSigning in FleetElasticityPolicy and restart gateway deployment.
